# Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] Kamino Swap is the execution layer for all Multiply flash-loan swaps (open, adjust, close) and uses multi-DEX routing to get the best output. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/products/swap · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts

## How it works

- [statement] In the Kamino SDK flow, slippagePct also sizes the flash loan so that the worst-case swap fill still covers the repayment. The swap quote's priceAInB must be the mid price (before slippage). Passing a minimum-out price counts slippage twice and sizes the position wrong. Slippage also absorbs the gap between the best quoted route and the route actually sent. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/repay-collateral-kswap · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/multiply-deleverage-xstocks
- [statement] Solana transaction size limits constrain which swap route a deleverage can use. Kamino's examples compress each KSwap route candidate with address lookup tables and send the first candidate that fits, sorted by best output. The best-output route often does not fit; in the docs' testing only one or two of five to ten routes did. The executed route can therefore be worse than the best quote, and the example code does not retry or fall back when no route fits. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/repay-collateral-kswap · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/multiply-deleverage-xstocks
- [statement] Kamino's docs say the amount of LSTs deposited across Solana DeFi far outweighs the liquidity in DEX pools, so moderate selling can cause a temporary market depeg; they name large DEX sell orders and Solana's roughly 2-day epoch unstaking delay as causes of dislocation. Inference: exit capacity for SOL LST loops is DEX depth plus whatever instant-unstake liquidity exists (for example the Sanctum Infinity reserve), not the headline supply of the LST. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/security/oracles/lst-oracles · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/risk/asset-risk/depeg, https://learn.sanctum.so/docs/technical-documentation/infinity

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] If the flash loan cannot be repaid (slippage beyond tolerance, insufficient liquidity, or any other failure), the whole Kamino Multiply transaction reverts and no state changes. A slippage tolerance that is too tight for the unwind size therefore shows up as a failed close, not as a partial fill. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/repay-collateral-kswap
- [statement] On the Kamino Swap page, price impact is computed before execution and shown with a warning at 1% or more and an error at 5% or more. Max slippage is a revert cap (the worked example uses 50 bps), the Swap product adds no platform fee, and it queries 15+ routing engines concurrently, with Jupiter/Metis, DFlow and OKX handling most volume. The page states no default tolerance and does not say whether Multiply closes apply the same warning thresholds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/products/swap · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging
- [statement] Inference from Kamino's docs: an atomic unwind needs idle cash in the reserves it touches. Kamino lists insufficient liquidity as a cause of flash loan revert, and its risk page says that at 100% utilization lenders cannot withdraw until borrowers repay or new supply arrives. A deleverage that needs more of the debt token or collateral than the reserve holds idle fails as a whole, or must be staged in smaller steps. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/risk
- [statement] Manual unwinding is the antipattern the flash-loan routes replace. Kamino's comparison (written for building loops) says manual looping takes 8-10 transactions, exposes the user to price moves between steps and slippage on every swap, while atomic Multiply has a single consolidated slippage check. The academic paper models stETH deleveraging as a repeated swap-repay-withdraw cycle on Curve, and BGD notes that health-factor limits can make a one-shot swap impossible without a flash loan. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2401.08610v4, https://governance.aave.com/t/bgd-aave-debt-swap-adapter-contract/12738
- [statement] Flash-loan deleveraging on Kamino is SDK-only. The docs say the Multiply helpers (getDepositWithLeverageIxs, getWithdrawWithLeverageIxs, getRepayWithCollIxs) exist only in the TypeScript SDK, the REST API cannot build flash loans, and the Rust klend-interface crate exposes flash-loan primitives but not the combo helpers. The examples pin @kamino-finance/kswap-sdk 2.9.0 with klend-sdk 13. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/multiply/overview · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts, https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/multiply-deleverage-xstocks
- [statement] Kamino can force a deleveraging. Its Risk Council may start auto-deleveraging, a systematic reduction of the largest leveraged positions, after a 72-hour warning to the affected positions; Kamino says it has never been triggered. The risk page lists auto-deleverage as the last step of its escalation path. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/products/multiply/risks · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/risk
- [statement] A Kamino Multiply unwind runs as one atomic transaction around a klend flash loan: flash-borrow one token, repay the debt, withdraw the freed collateral, swap collateral to the debt token through KSwap, repay the flash loan, and pay the remainder to the wallet (the order of swap and repay depends on the flash shape, see the next claim). If the swap or any other step leaves the flash repay short, the whole transaction reverts and no state changes. The klend program enforces the pairing on-chain by reading the transaction's instruction list: a flash borrow must be followed in the same transaction by exactly one matching flash repay (same amount, same accounts, correct borrow-instruction index), a second flash borrow in the transaction is rejected with 'Multiple flash borrows not allowed', a missing repay fails with 'No flash repay found', and neither instruction may be called through CPI. A wrapper program therefore cannot hold a Kamino flash loan open on its own, and one flash-loan unwind cannot span transactions (a larger unwind has to be several separate flash-loan transactions). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-19) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/repay-collateral-kswap · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://github.com/Kamino-Finance/klend/blob/77e81854909ab7ffea3a2e898b2554d96e07daac/programs/klend/src/lending_market/flash_ixs.rs, https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/multiply/leverage-concepts
- [statement] A flash-loan unwind needs idle cash in the flash-borrowed reserve, and the SDK refuses to build the transaction when neither reserve has it. determineFlashBorrowType requires flash loans to be enabled on the reserve and enough available liquidity: for coll-flash the collateral reserve must cover the flash borrow plus the collateral redeemed in the same transaction, for debt-flash the debt reserve must cover the whole repay amount. The code comments that a thin collateral reserve can satisfy the flash borrow alone yet still revert with InsufficientLiquidity (klend error 6008) once the redeem is added on top, and that debt-flash is the safe choice for thin or nascent LST reserves on withdraw or close. If neither side qualifies it throws 'Neither collateral nor debt reserve supports flash borrowing the required amount'. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://github.com/Kamino-Finance/klend-sdk/blob/6a26d6f1b5afb29953ffd139ee8c0c4ca5f26ce6/src/leverage/utils.ts · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://github.com/Kamino-Finance/klend-sdk/blob/6a26d6f1b5afb29953ffd139ee8c0c4ca5f26ce6/src/leverage/flashBorrowType.ts
- [statement] Kamino values SOL LST collateral at the stake-pool exchange rate, not the DEX price, so a market depeg changes neither LTV nor liquidation status. Its docs state the assumptions behind that: LST deposits across Solana DeFi far outweigh DEX liquidity, arbitrageurs are expected to buy a discounted LST and unstake it, and if arbitrage fails (for example a stake pool bug that blocks unstaking) the protocol could hold collateral valued above what the market will pay, with any bad debt socialized among lenders in the affected market. The Multiply risk table lists SOL LST depeg risk as 'Eliminated (stake oracle)' and borrow-rate risk as the primary risk. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/security/oracles/lst-oracles · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://kamino.com/docs/products/multiply/risks

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Jupiter Lend flash loans carry no fee. Its developer docs say to 'Return the same borrowed amount to Jupiter Lend (no fees)', and its user docs say the Multiply flash loan shows 'Flash Loan Fee: Free' and that Unwind adds no protocol fee and also uses a free flash loan. The user's cost is the swap: the docs state that each Multiply or Unwind swaps tokens through Jupiter, so the user bears price impact and route fees. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/flashloan.md · keywords: Unwind cost slippage and flash loan deleveraging · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/lend/multiply
